Hi all — quick finance notes after reviewing ACME_SOW_v2.pdf and the initial ask: 

1) Mixed SKU approach is supported: we can publish two product codes under one listing (seats = subscription SKU, compute = metered SKU). Reporting will provide per-product usage so Acme can reconcile.
2) Trial -> paid conversion: recommended approach is to create a non-billable entitlement for the trial (Marketplace entitlement flag) and then switch to the billable SKU on conversion. Important: Marketplace records entitlement changes asynchronously — expect up to a 5-minute lag for immediate conversions, and up to 24 hours for bulk/edge-case reconciliations.
3) Proration: Marketplace-level proration semantics vary by product listing (we can support start-of-cycle proration or full-cycle proration). Procurement should confirm which they prefer. Default is pro-rate to the remaining cycle for seat changes.
4) Overages & disputed usage: we need a dispute window (recommended 30 days) and webhooks must expose a deterministic event id for idempotency.

I've attached a sample pricing-mapping.csv with column headers: product_code, meter_dimension, reporting_interval, price_per_unit, billing_cycle. Please review and confirm values for "Acme Core" and "Acme Compute."

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace onboarding — technical notes on metering webhooks and edge cases

Sam / team — technical follow-up after reviewing the MAF and trial-flow diagram. Key implementation notes and edge cases we should align on: 

- Webhook delivery & retries: Redwood will send usage events to the Marketplace via the standard seller API. If Marketplace ack fails, Redwood will retry with exponential backoff for up to 72 hours and persist events for reconciliation. We also include a numeric event id and HMAC signature for idempotency and verification.
- Entitlement creation during trial: We'll provision a read-only entitlement flag in the Marketplace as a non-billable object. On conversion we promote the entitlement to the billable SKU and send a promotion event. There is an edge case where a conversion and immediate usage occur within seconds; we'll attempt synchronous promotion but accept the 0–5 minute window Ben called out. Please note: some downstream billing connectors apply cutoff windows (midnight UTC), which could shift charges to the following cycle.
- Combined SKU reporting: If a single order contains both seats and compute usage, Redwood will emit two separate meter records with the same order_id to allow Acme to reconcile per-order.
- Revocation & suspension: If Acme requests revocation for a user during dispute, Marketplace revocation can take up to 24 hours to reflect — Redwood supports immediate local enforcement (block requests) when we receive a revocation API call, but Marketplace front-end may still show the product until entitlement sync completes.

Next steps: 
1) Monica: confirm go/no-go for a canary listing (small % of customers) week of 6/14.
2) Sam: confirm preferred proration behavior and provide final SOW redline acceptance if possible.
3) Ben / Aditya / Karthik: we'll schedule a 30-min technical/pricing sync on 6/2 at 10:00 PT (per Monica's options) unless procurement requests otherwise.
